conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I understand you've been having abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. Can you tell me more about what’s been going on?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it’s been getting worse over the past week. The pain is mostly in my upper right side, and I’ve been vomiting a lot. I think it’s another partial bowel blockage.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That sounds familiar. Given your history of Crohn’s and multiple surgeries, that’s definitely possible. You came in with an NG tube already placed?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, they put it in at the outside hospital. It helps a little, but the pain is still bad.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll keep the NG tube for now to help with the vomiting. Your labs show your kidney function is a bit off—creatinine is elevated to 1.6, which is higher than your baseline.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, that’s not good. Is it from dehydration?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Likely, especially with vomiting and not keeping fluids down. We’re giving IV fluids and also replaced some magnesium, which was low.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that makes sense. What about pain control? I need something, but I know you’re cautious.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we are being careful. You’ve had issues in the past with sedation from Dilaudid, and our system flags that. We can give 1 mg IV every 3 hours if needed, but no more.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I understand. I just want to be safe. I don’t want another Narcan incident like before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. We’re monitoring closely. For now, we’ll stick to the plan and reassess your pain regularly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your blood culture came back — no growth, which is good. No sign of bloodstream infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. I was worried about infection with everything going on.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll keep an eye on it. Your urine culture showed mixed bacteria, but it looks like contamination, not a real UTI.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, okay. I thought maybe that could be causing the fever I had.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The fever might just be from the inflammation in your gut. We’re not seeing signs of active infection so far.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How are you feeling today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Still nauseous, but maybe a little less pain. The NG tube is uncomfortable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I know it’s not comfortable, but it’s helping your stomach rest. We’ll keep it until we’re sure things are moving again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Any update on the imaging?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not yet. We’re planning a repeat abdominal X-ray tomorrow to see if the obstruction is improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We did a chest X-ray yesterday to check your NG tube placement. It’s in the right spot, in the stomach.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good. Is everything else okay?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: There was a new finding — a small area of consolidation in your right upper lung, possibly early pneumonia.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Pneumonia? I haven’t had a cough or fever lately.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Sometimes it shows up on X-ray before symptoms. We’ll monitor you closely. No antibiotics yet unless you develop symptoms.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, just keep me posted.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great news — your repeat abdominal X-ray shows the bowel dilation is gone. No signs of obstruction anymore.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Really? That’s amazing! Does that mean I can eat soon?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll start with small sips of water today. If you tolerate that, we can slowly advance your diet.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And can we take out the NG tube?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: If you do well with liquids, we can remove it tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well with sips. No nausea or vomiting. We’re going to try clear liquids now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. I’m so ready to eat something real.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: One step at a time. We also got your second blood culture back — still no growth. That’s reassuring.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Morning. You made it through the night with clear liquids. No issues?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, I feel good. Can we take the NG tube out now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll remove it this morning. After that, we’ll try a soft diet and keep monitoring.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I’ve missed eating so much.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re tolerating the soft diet well. Your kidney function is also improving — creatinine is down to 1.1.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. Does that mean I can go home soon?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Possibly tomorrow. We want to make sure you’re stable on food and pain is controlled with oral meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been using the IV Dilaudid. Will I switch to pills?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll transition you to oral hydromorphone. Same strength, but safer at home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing really well. We’re planning to discharge you tomorrow afternoon if all goes well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s wonderful. What about follow-up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll need to see your GI doctor soon. Also, we’ll schedule a pneumonia follow-up chest X-ray in a week.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my other meds — thyroid, blood pressure, depression?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, resume all your home medications. We’ll send prescriptions and instructions with you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve made it through the night with no issues. We’re clearing you for discharge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you so much. I feel so much better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll give you a summary, prescriptions, and instructions. Call your doctor if pain returns or you can’t keep food down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. And thank you for being careful with the pain meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We want you safe and comfortable. Take care, and we’ll see you in follow-up if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: One last thing — we’re due for your flu shot. Would you like it before you leave?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I haven’t had it this year. Is it safe with everything?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it’s recommended. No live virus. We’ll give it before you go.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Flu shot is in. All set for discharge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. I’m ready to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Transport is scheduled for 1 PM. Nurse will go over meds and signs to watch for.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Dr. Lee. I really appreciate everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care of yourself and follow up as planned.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just checking in before you leave. Any last questions?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, I think I’ve got everything. Thanks again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Safe travels home. We’ll see you in clinic if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll be in touch if anything comes up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. You did great.
